description: qou-99qc: the augmentation IS the Markov trace at z = q (unique), so the two admissible Q_beta functionals differ only in the Markov parameter. By block support the augmentation is a ONE-row truncation and z_D the TWO-row one; D7 (2026-09-07) scopes convention D -- the two-row TL truncation -- to the decay/Q_beta channel, which selects z_D. Scope-(a); wires nothing.

checks.name: augmentation_IS_the_markov_trace_at_z_equals_q
checks.detail: all 6 basis elements of H_3(q) agree: the Markov trace built from tr(1)=1, tr(x s_n)=z tr(x), cyclicity and s^2 = h s + 1, evaluated at z = q, equals the algebra map s_i -> q. The 'multiplicative functional vs Markov trace' dichotomy the corpus has been carrying is FALSE

checks.name: and_z_equals_q_is_the_UNIQUE_such_parameter
checks.detail: solving for basis-wide agreement over an unrestricted z gives exactly [q] -- so the augmentation is ONE POINT of the Markov family, not a functional of a different kind that happens to collide somewhere

checks.name: CALIBRATION_y_1cubed_vanishes_at_EXACTLY_the_known_two_roots
checks.detail: solving y_(1,1,1)(z) = 0 gives [q, q**3/(q**2 + 1)] = {q, q^3/(q^2+1)}, the two admissible parameters the corpus already establishes by an independent route. A wrong character table or normalisation would not reproduce that pair, so the table below is checked against the corpus, not asserted

checks.name: conventionD_is_the_TWO_ROW_family_lambda_eq_n_minus_k_k
checks.detail: z_D is supported on [(2, 1), (3,)] = {(3-0,0), (3-1,1)} with y_(1,1,1) = 0 -- exactly D7's stated characterisation of convention D as the two-row TL truncation (TemperleyLiebTower's concrete lambda = (n-k,k))

checks.name: augmentation_is_STRICTLY_FINER_a_ONE_ROW_truncation
checks.detail: the augmentation is supported on [(3,)] alone -- it kills (2,1) as well as (1,1,1), so it is a ONE-row truncation, a proper refinement of D rather than D itself. Therefore it is NOT the convention-D functional

checks.name: D7_count_trap_is_REAL_here_and_this_probe_avoids_it
checks.detail: rows<=2 and cols<=2 both give dimension sum 5 = catalan(3), so a count-based labelling cannot tell the row reading from the column one (D7's transposition-blindness trap). Nothing above counts: every claim is about WHICH partitions carry nonzero weight

checks.name: CALIBRATION_reproduces_the_merged_two_cells
checks.detail: 12.47002366 % and -43.15717469 % reproduce the +12.470 % / -43.157 % of #6722/#6763/#6832, so the machinery here is anchored to the merged numbers rather than free-standing

caveats: Scope-(a). Establishes an identification and a block-support fact; it does not derive Q_beta and proposes no value for anything.
The selected functional gives the WORSE residual (-43.157 % vs +12.470 %). That is the anti-fitting directive working, not a defect.

Option E -- derive a different element Delta -- is untouched and remains the only route to a parameter-free admissible sub-1 % result (qou-37j2). Commit 5f5cdebef5b showed that search is real: eps(Delta_S) and chi_(3)(Delta_L) are genuinely different elements, not an arithmetic discrepancy.
The n = 3 computation is the Q_beta ladder's H_3, which is the algebra D7 names for this channel. Nothing here is claimed for general n.
